Hi Ava — great, thanks for confirming for Mar 16. Quick heads up on cross-region DST: the US switches to daylight time on Sun, 8 Mar 2026 (clocks forward), and Australia stops daylight time on Sun, 5 Apr 2026 (clocks back). For single sessions that's fine, but for any recurring or follow-up meeting around the April week you mentioned, participants in Sydney may see the meeting appear an hour earlier on their calendars after Apr 5 if the invite was created before the changeover.

I want to avoid confusion for your engineers. We have two options for the early-April follow-up:

1) Keep the original UTC anchor (so the meeting will shift local times when DST changes) — simplest if everyone is OK adjusting local clocks.
2) Force a new invite that fixes the local Sydney time we want (e.g., 11:00 AM AEST on Tue 6 Apr) so Sydney participants see the same local time both before and after the Southern DST change — this requires re-issuing the invite so other regions will see a different UTC time.

If you want, I can propose two alternative slots that keep the working-hours overlap without straddling both changeovers. Suggested windows (all local times shown):
- Option A: Tue, 6 Apr 2026 at 11:00 AM AEST / Mon, 5 Apr 2026 8:00 PM PDT / Mon, 5 Apr 2026 11:00 PM EDT
- Option B: Wed, 7 Apr 2026 at 09:00 AM AEST / Tue, 6 Apr 2026 6:00 PM PDT / Tue, 6 Apr 2026 9:00 PM EDT

If you prefer the follow-up to remain at the same UTC time instead, let me know and I won't re-issue invites. I can also loop in Rishi if we need to make it a formal recurring series.

Thanks — want me to propose the new invite now?

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
